Options: [I have been a lifelong competitive athlete. | I have had phases of high activity mixed with other life pursuits. | I am looking to establish a serious, high-performance rhythm for the first time.]

Reflecting on your decades of experience, which of these domains best captures the core focus that defined your athletic journey?
Options: [Endurance and long-distance disciplines | High-intensity, explosive team athletics | Strength, power, and precision-based training | I have cycled through a wide variety of disciplines]

As you look toward the next chapter of your high-performance athletic journey, what is the primary motivation driving you to push your limits right now?
Options: [Testing my physical peak at this stage in life. | Seeking a new discipline to master from the ground up. | Mentoring others while staying actively involved in high-performance sport. | Maintaining elite standards in a field I am already established in.]

scouting_result.scout_verdict:
Your history as a lifelong competitive athlete, combined with your focus on strength and power, has built the chassis of a pure sprinter. At 178cm and 78kg, you possess the structural density that, when coupled with refined acceleration mechanics, translates directly to the track. While some might see 45 as a stage for winding down, you are choosing to lean into the explosive nature of the Block Starter—an archetype defined by the kinetic snap of the first ten meters.

Stepping into this role at The Brisbane 2032 Games represents more than just a race; it is a test of your ability to master the biomechanical nuances of high-velocity movement. You are no longer relying on old habits; you are treating the block start as a brand-new scientific endeavor. By focusing on the intersection of your power-based history and the precision required for high-performance sprinting, you transform the track into your laboratory, aiming to prove that the peak is a state of mind as much as it is a physiological measurement.

scouting_result.pathway_adaptive: Para-Alpine Skiing (e.g., Men's Super-G Sit-Ski LW12)
scouting_result.scout_verdict:
The Edge Carver archetype calls for a precise blend of physical control and high-speed geometry. With your background in power-based training, you have the raw materials to translate that force into the tight, controlled lines of the slopes. This path isn't just about speed; it is about the mastery of friction and momentum—the same focus you have always applied to your training, now redirected into a high-velocity, technical environment where every fraction of a degree in your posture shifts your trajectory.

At The French Alps 2030 Games, you will find that your desire for a new discipline to master is met with the unforgiving, beautiful complexity of Alpine skiing. Your 45-year history of athletic dedication provides the grit required to navigate the learning curve of this precision-based field. You aren't just carving ice; you are sculpting your legacy through a discipline that demands your total mental and physical presence, proving that for a true athlete, the most exciting challenge is always the one you have not yet mastered.

eval_result.summary: The narrative successfully integrates the user's age, biometrics, and interview answers into a compelling narrative, though starting elite sprinting or alpine skiing from scratch at age 45 stretches real-world authenticity.

distinctness.reasoning: The two archetypes offer vastly different sport families (summer track vs. winter alpine) and provide solid adaptive analogues for both.
